reviewQuestions: Does the methodology cover relevant fundamental rights?
Does it preserve FRIA as distinct from a GDPR/LED/EUDPR DPIA while allowing controlled cross-reference and factual reuse?
Are consultation and mitigation requirements explicit?
scope: FRIA/DPIA separation, overlap control and permissible cross-reference/reuse
officialSources: Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union

preReviewFindings.finding: Applicability depends on deployer category, Annex III context and actual use context.
preReviewFindings.requiredDecision: Approve applicability questions and mandatory escalation cases.

preReviewFindings.finding: Rights and affected-group taxonomies are decision support, not an exhaustive legal analysis.
preReviewFindings.requiredDecision: Confirm minimum rights coverage and required contextual additions.

preReviewFindings.finding: FRIA is a distinct fundamental-rights accountability assessment and must not be represented as replaced by a data-protection DPIA. Where personal-data processing overlaps, evidence or relevant DPIA sections may be cross-referenced/reused without silently collapsing the two assessments.
preReviewFindings.requiredDecision: Approve the FRIA/DPIA separation, reuse rules and customer-facing explanation.

preReviewFindings.finding: Stakeholder consultation and notification operating commitments are not established repository facts.
preReviewFindings.requiredDecision: Define product wording and customer-responsibility boundary after founder input.

acceptanceCriteria: Relevant rights, groups, impacts and mitigations are covered.
FRIA remains distinct from DPIA while avoiding unnecessary duplication where cross-reference is legally appropriate.
Residual high impact cannot be auto-approved.
Consultation and notification boundaries are explicit.
humanInputsRequired: privacy counsel/DPO input where DPIA overlap is material
limitations: The platform cannot identify every affected group without customer facts.
A FRIA does not replace a legally required DPIA, and a DPIA does not automatically satisfy Article 27.
Residual-impact acceptability is a human decision.
